newsitem.title: USA: Aleutian volcano erupts with ash spurt.
newsitem.headline: Aleutian volcano erupts with ash spurt.

text.p: A volcano on one of Alaska's Aleutian Islands erupted on Thursday with a cloud of dark ash that rose to 5,000 feet (1,500 metres) before dissipating, officials said.
Umnak Island's Okmok Volcano, about 875 miles (1,400 km) southwest of Anchorage, coughed out its ash plume late in the morning, said officials from the Alaska Volcano Observatory.

The nearest settlements are Nikolski, an Aleut village of about 35 located 45 miles (70 km) west of the volcano, and a handful of people staying at an abandoned military base 10 miles (16 km) east of the island and who reported the eruption, the observatory said.

There have been no reports of ashfall in Nikolski or nearbly Unalaska, said Tom Miller, active scientist-in-charge at the volcano observatory. Winds appear to be carrying any ash away from settlements, he said.

Okmok, which rises to 3,520 feet (1,073 metres), has a six-mile (9.6 km) wide crater that occupies most of the eastern end of Umnak Island. It has had frequent but relatively undramatic and intermittent eruptions, the observatory said. The last eruptive period lasted from November 1986 to February 1988.
Thursday's eruption could mark the start of a similar period, Miller said.
"It's a fairly active volcano. This could be the start of a relatively long-lived eruption that's sporadic in nature," he said.
In 1945 a "fairly rigorous" burst sent ash up to 45,000 feet (14,000 metres), but most Okmok eruptions are small, Miller said.
Rising to only 5,000 feet (1,500 metres), Thursday's ash cloud posed little danger to passing aircraft, he said.
